examples.ko: 이 아파트 거주민들은 주차 문제로 모였어요.
examples.en: The residents of this apartment complex gathered over the parking problem.
Most of the people living in this village are elderly.

examples.ko: 새로 생긴 공원 덕분에 거주민들의 만족도가 높아졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the new park, residents' satisfaction has gone up.
The city handed out garbage bags to the residents.

examples.ko: 이 섬의 거주민은 백 명도 안 돼요.
examples.en: This island has fewer than a hundred inhabitants.

examples.ko: 거주민 우선 주차 구역이라서 외부 차는 세울 수 없어요.
examples.en: It's a residents-first parking zone, so outside cars can't park.

explain: '주민'이 더 일상적이고, '거주민'은 어떤 지역에 살고 있다는 점을 강조하는 말투예요. 공고문과 뉴스에서 잘 보여요. '원주민'은 원래부터 살던 사람이라서 '거주민'과 뜻이 달라요.

phrases.en: The residents cleaned the park together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거주민'보다 일상적이고 더 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday and more common than 거주민.

phrases.en: Local residents get a parking discount.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 지역에 사는 사람을 가리킬 때 앞에 '지역'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 지역 points to people living in that area.

phrases.en: It's a parking lot only residents can use.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공고문에서 사는 사람으로 제한할 때 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in notices that limit something to residents.

explain_en: '주민' is more everyday, while '거주민' stresses the fact that someone lives in an area. It shows up in notices and news. '원주민' means people who lived there originally, so it differs from '거주민'.

examples.ko: 거짓말을 같이 덮어 준 저도 공범자가 된 기분이에요.
examples.en: I feel like an accomplice too, since I helped cover up the lie.
In the movie, the main character drew his friend in as an accomplice.

examples.ko: 공범자는 아직 잡히지 않았다고 뉴스에서 말했어요.
examples.en: The news said the accomplice has not been caught yet.
The accomplices in the fraud case stood in court.

examples.ko: 장난을 같이 친 공범자끼리 눈짓을 주고받았어요.
examples.en: The partners in crime of the prank exchanged glances.
Everyone who knows the secret is an accomplice.

explain: 줄여서 '공범'이라고도 많이 말해요. 뉴스뿐 아니라 친구끼리 비밀이나 장난을 같이 할 때 농담으로 '우리 공범이야'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The police are looking for the accomplice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공범자'를 줄인 말로 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 공범자, more common in conversation.

phrases.en: If you help with a lie, you become an accomplice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일에 함께하게 되는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes being drawn into doing something wrong together.

phrases.en: I did nothing, but I was treated as an accomplice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰리다'는 억울하게 그런 사람으로 여겨질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '몰리다' suggests being unfairly regarded as one.

explain_en: It is often shortened to '공범'. Besides the news, friends sometimes use it jokingly when sharing a secret or a prank, as in '우리 공범이야'.

examples.ko: 그 지역의 권력가가 사업에 영향을 줬다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a rumor that a powerful person in that region influenced the business.

examples.ko: 권력가와 친하다고 해서 모든 일이 풀리지는 않아요.
examples.en: Being close to a powerful person doesn't solve everything.
In dramas, powerful figures usually appear as villains.

examples.ko: 그는 힘 있는 권력가의 아들로 태어났어요.
examples.en: He was born the son of a powerful man.

examples.ko: 권력가에게 잘 보이려고 애쓰는 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people try hard to win favor with the powerful.

examples.ko: 권력가들이 모인 자리에서 이 문제가 논의됐어요.
examples.en: This issue was discussed at a gathering of powerful people.

explain: '권력자'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰고 뉴스나 드라마 이야기에서 나와요. '재력가'처럼 '-가'가 붙은 짝말도 있어요.

phrases.en: I heard the person in power in that country has changed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권력가와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 뉴스나 이야기에서 모두 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 권력가; common in news and stories.

phrases.example: 권력가의 아들이라는 이유로 특별한 대우를 받았어요.
phrases.en: He got special treatment because he was the son of a powerful person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권력가의 가족을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for talking about the family of a powerful person.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 권력가와 손잡고 사업을 키웠어요.
phrases.en: That company grew its business by teaming up with a powerful person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘 있는 사람과 가까워지는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone gets close to or allies with a powerful person.
phrases.en_equiv: to team up with a powerful person

explain_en: It is used almost the same way as '권력자' and appears in news and drama stories. There is a matching word with '-가', '재력가' (a wealthy person).

examples.en: I'm a Christian, so I go to church every Sunday.

examples.ko: 기독교인의 가정에서 자라서 성경 이야기를 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: I grew up in a Christian family, so I heard a lot of Bible stories.
He is a Christian, but he respects other religions too.
My mother is a devout Christian.
There are many Christian students at this school.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 기독교인이 된 지 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been five years since my friend became a Christian.

explain: '크리스천'이라고도 많이 말하고, '기독교 신자'나 '신자'도 비슷하게 써요. 한국에서 '기독교'는 흔히 개신교를 가리킬 때가 많아서, 천주교는 '천주교 신자'나 '가톨릭 신자'라고 따로 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: My friend is a Christian.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 많이 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual word often used in daily talk.

phrases.en: My whole family are Christians.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신자'를 붙이면 믿는 사람이라는 뜻이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 신자 makes it clear the person is a believer.

phrases.en: I became a Christian in college.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿음을 갖게 된 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about coming to faith.

explain_en: People also say '크리스천', and '기독교 신자' or '신자' are used in a similar way. In Korea '기독교' often refers to Protestantism, so Catholics are often called '천주교 신자' or '가톨릭 신자' separately.

examples.en: During the holidays, everyone heads off to their hometowns.

examples.ko: 사람들이 너나없이 그 노래를 따라 불렀어요.
examples.en: Everyone sang along to that song.
These days everyone is just staring at their phones.
The villagers all came out and helped.
Everyone is busy these days, aren't they?
During exam season, everybody goes to the library.

explain: '누구나 다'처럼 예외 없이 모두를 말할 때 써요. '너나 할 것 없이'와 같은 뜻이고, 말하는 사람이 사람들의 공통된 모습을 짚어 이야기할 때 잘 나와요.

phrases.example: 너나 할 것 없이 다들 지쳐 있었어요.
phrases.en: Everyone, without exception, was exhausted.
phrases.nuance_ko: '너나없이'와 같은 뜻으로, 말할 때 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'neonaeopsi', and heard more often in speech.

phrases.en: Everyone knows this song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 말로 모두를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier phrase for referring to everyone.

phrases.en: When the sale started, everyone rushed to the store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모든 사람이 같은 행동을 할 때 동사와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a verb when everyone does the same action.

explain_en: It means everyone without exception, like '누구나 다'. It has the same meaning as '너나 할 것 없이' and comes up when pointing out something people all have in common.

examples.ko: 요즘 젊은 사람들이 너도나도 그 사업에 달려들고 있어요.
examples.en: These days young people are all jumping into that business.

examples.ko: 신제품이 나오자 사람들이 너도나도 사려고 했어요.
examples.en: When the new product came out, everyone wanted to buy it.
Everybody is talking only about stocks.
In the classroom, the students all raised their hands.
It's moving season, so everyone is going around looking at houses.
The students all took part in the volunteer work.

explain: '모두'와 달리 서로서로 따라 하며 한꺼번에 몰리는 분위기를 보여 줘요. 유행이나 인기, 몰려드는 상황에서 잘 쓰고 뒤에는 보통 동작이 와요.

phrases.en: Everyone, without exception, sang along to that song.
phrases.nuance_ko: '너도나도'와 비슷하게 모두가 그렇다는 뜻이에요. 조금 더 글 같은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '너도나도', meaning everyone; slightly more formal in feel.

phrases.en: When the restaurant became famous, people all flocked to it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인기 있는 곳에 사람이 한꺼번에 모이는 장면에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many people gather at a popular place at once.

phrases.en: Since my friend did it, everyone followed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유행처럼 서로 따라 하는 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a trend where everyone copies each other.

explain_en: Unlike '모두', it shows a mood of people copying each other and crowding in all at once. It suits trends, popularity and rushes, and an action usually follows it.

examples.ko: 이 놀이공원은 남녀노소 누구나 즐길 수 있는 놀이 기구가 많아요.
examples.en: This amusement park has many rides that anyone, young or old, can enjoy.

examples.ko: 이 메뉴는 남녀노소 선호도가 높아서 단체 주문에 많이 시켜요.
examples.en: This menu item is popular with all ages, so it's often ordered for groups.
Regardless of age, health is the most important thing.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 남녀노소가 다 아는 노래예요.
examples.en: This is a song that everybody, young and old, knows.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 노소 구분 없이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: People in our neighborhood get along regardless of age.

examples.ko: 마을 잔치에서는 노소 할 것 없이 함께 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: At the village festival, young and old danced together.

explain: 거의 '남녀노소'라는 말로 굳어서 써요. '노소'만 쓸 때는 '노소를 막론하고', '노소 구분 없이'처럼 나이와 상관없다는 뜻의 말과 함께 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 축제는 남녀노소 누구나 즐길 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This festival can be enjoyed by anyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남자, 여자, 늙은이, 젊은이를 나란히 말해서 '모든 사람'이라는 뜻이 돼요. 광고나 안내문, 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It lines up men, women, old and young to mean 'everybody'. You often hear it in ads, notices and the news.

explain_en: It is used almost entirely as part of the set phrase '남녀노소'. On its own it appears in phrases that mean 'regardless of age', such as '노소를 막론하고' and '노소 구분 없이'.

examples.en: You shouldn't scorn people like that.

examples.ko: 그 기사는 노동자를 능멸하는 표현이 많아서 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: That article was criticized for its many expressions that disdain workers.

examples.ko: 친구가 저를 능멸했다고 생각해서 너무 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I thought my friend had scorned me, so I got really angry.

examples.ko: 일부러 상대를 능멸하려고 한 말은 아니었어요.
examples.en: I didn't say it on purpose to belittle the other person.

examples.ko: 국민을 능멸한다는 말이 나올 정도로 사과가 늦었어요.
examples.en: The apology came so late that people said it showed contempt for the public.

examples.ko: 저를 능멸하지 마세요. 저도 최선을 다했어요.
examples.en: Don't look down on me. I did my best too.

explain: '무시하다'보다 훨씬 강해서 상대를 깔보고 자존심을 짓밟는다는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스, 글, 화가 난 말에서 주로 나오고 평소 대화에서는 '무시하다'나 '깔보다'를 더 많이 써요. '국민을 능멸하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: You shouldn't look down on people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but easier and more everyday.

phrases.en: The citizens felt they had been insulted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능멸을 받는 쪽에서 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive expression from the viewpoint of the one scorned.

phrases.en: Remarks that scorn the weak become a problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발언', '표현'과 같이 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with words like remark in writing and news.

explain_en: It is much stronger than '무시하다' and carries the feeling of looking down on someone and trampling their pride. It appears mainly in news, writing and angry speech, while in everyday talk people use '무시하다' or '깔보다'. It is used with an object, as in '국민을 능멸하다'.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 뜨내기손님보다 단골이 더 많아요.
examples.en: This shop has more regulars than one-time customers.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 뜨내기라서 이 동네 사정을 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: He's just passing through, so he doesn't know much about this neighborhood.

examples.ko: 뜨내기 일꾼을 구해서 하루만 일을 맡겼어요.
examples.en: I found a drifter for day work and gave him the job for just one day.

examples.ko: 우리 가게는 뜨내기손님한테도 늘 친절하게 대해요.
examples.en: Our shop is always kind even to customers who just stop by once.

examples.ko: 뜨내기라고 해서 함부로 대하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't treat someone carelessly just because they're a drifter.
At big construction sites, transient workers often come and go.

explain: 한곳에 자리 잡지 않고 떠도는 사람을 말하고, 장사하는 곳에서는 가끔 한 번 들르는 손님을 가리켜요. 반대로 자주 오는 손님은 '단골'이라고 해요. 사람에게 직접 쓰면 낮춰 보는 느낌이 있어서 조심해야 해요.

phrases.en: Restaurants in tourist areas get many one-time customers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가끔 한 번 들르는 손님을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for customers who only stop by once in a while.

phrases.en: This shop has about half drop-ins and half regulars.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단골'과 반대로 놓고 비교할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often set against '단골' (regular) for comparison.

phrases.example: 이 동네는 뜨내기가 많아서 서로 잘 몰라요.
phrases.en: Many people here come and go, so neighbors don't know each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리 잡지 않고 떠도는 사람이 많다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means many people come and go without settling.

explain_en: It refers to a person who drifts without settling down, and in business it means a customer who only drops in occasionally. The opposite is '단골' (regular customer). Using it directly about a person can sound belittling, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 지원금은 미혼자도 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Unmarried people can apply for this subsidy too.
Both unmarried and married people took part in the survey.
The proportion of unmarried people is growing every year.

examples.ko: 이 기숙사는 미혼자만 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only unmarried people can move into this dormitory.

examples.ko: 미혼자라고 해서 결혼 생각이 없는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because someone is unmarried doesn't mean they have no thoughts of marrying.

examples.ko: 신청서에 미혼자는 이 칸을 비워 두세요.
examples.en: If you are unmarried, leave this box blank on the form.

explain: 서류, 통계, 뉴스에서 '기혼자'와 짝으로 자주 나와요. 평소 대화에서는 '미혼'이나 '결혼 안 한 사람'이라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. 사람을 직접 부를 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I'm still unmarried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 소개나 대화에서는 '미혼자'보다 '미혼'이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In conversation or self-introductions, '미혼' sounds more natural than '미혼자'.

phrases.en: The survey asked married and unmarried people separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통계나 서류에서 두 말이 짝으로 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two terms appear as a pair in statistics and forms.

phrases.en: This gathering is for unmarried people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모집 글이나 안내문에서 대상을 밝힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices to say who the target group is.

explain_en: It appears in forms, statistics and news as the pair of '기혼자' (married person). In everyday talk people often say '미혼' or '결혼 안 한 사람'. You would not use it to address someone directly.

examples.ko: 이 부대에는 민간인이 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Civilians cannot enter this military unit.
My father became a civilian after finishing the army.
Civilian casualties were large during the war.
I watched the training as a civilian.
The civilians evacuated to a safe place.
Soldiers and civilians dress differently.

explain: 민간인은 군인이나 경찰이 아닌 일반 사람이에요. 군대 이야기에서 '군인'과 짝으로 쓰고, 일상에서는 '일반인'이 더 흔해요. 전쟁 뉴스에서 '민간인 피해'라는 말이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Civilian casualties are the greatest in a war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전쟁이나 사건 뉴스에서 가장 자주 듣는 합친 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The compound heard most often in news about wars and incidents.

phrases.example: 군 부대 앞에 민간인 출입 금지 표지판이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a no-civilians-allowed sign in front of the military base.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대나 특별한 구역의 안내판에서 볼 수 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression seen on signs at military bases or restricted areas.

phrases.example: 이 행사는 일반인도 참가할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Ordinary people can also take part in this event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '민간인'보다 '일반인'을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, 일반인 is used more often than 민간인.

explain_en: 민간인 is an ordinary person who is not a soldier or police officer. It pairs with 군인 (soldier) in military talk; in daily life 일반인 is more common. News about war often says '민간인 피해' (civilian casualties).

examples.ko: 다른 사람의 외모를 비하하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't demean other people's looks.

examples.ko: 그 방송인은 특정 지역을 비하해서 사과했어요.
examples.en: That broadcaster apologized for disparaging a certain region.
Don't put yourself down; have some confidence.

examples.ko: 직업을 비하하는 말은 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best not to use words that belittle someone's job.

examples.ko: 친구가 나를 비하한 것 같아서 속상했어요.
examples.en: I felt upset because it seemed my friend looked down on me.
I had no intention of putting the other person down.

explain: '비하하다'는 남이나 자신을 실제보다 낮게 말해서 깎아내릴 때 써요. '무시하다'는 신경 쓰지 않는 것이고, '비하하다'는 말로 낮추는 것이에요. '자기 비하'처럼 자신에게도 쓰고, 뉴스에서는 '비하 발언'이라는 말이 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 자기 비하는 하지 않는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: It's better not to put yourself down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신을 낮추는 것을 가리키는 명사로, '하다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for belittling yourself, often used with 'hada'.

phrases.example: 그 사람의 비하 발언 때문에 논란이 됐어요.
phrases.en: His belittling remark caused controversy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 깎아내리는 말을 뉴스에서 이렇게 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: The way news reports refer to demeaning remarks.

phrases.en: Don't put yourself down. You did well enough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신이나 남을 낮춰 말하지 말라고 부드럽게 말릴 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to tell someone not to belittle themselves or others.

explain_en: 비하하다 is used for running someone, including yourself, down by speaking of them as lower than they are. 무시하다 is ignoring or not caring, while 비하하다 is lowering someone with words. It works for yourself too, as in 자기 비하, and 비하 발언 is common in the news.

examples.en: That mountaineer climbed to the top of Everest.
The mountaineers gathered and took safety training.
I went to hear a famous mountaineer's lecture.
My dream is to become a mountaineer.
I asked a mountaineer how to choose hiking boots.
My friend said she respects mountaineers.

explain: 주로 높은 산을 오르는 것을 전문적으로 하거나 깊이 즐기는 사람을 말해요. 가볍게 산에 가는 사람은 '등산객'이라고 하는 것이 자연스러워요. 뉴스에서 유명한 등반가를 소개할 때도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I read a book by a famous mountaineer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산악인'은 이렇게 앞에 꾸미는 말을 붙여 사람을 소개할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '산악인' is often introduced with a describing word like this.

phrases.example: 저는 어른이 되면 산악인이 되고 싶어요.
phrases.en: When I grow up, I want to become a mountaineer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산을 오르는 일을 직업이나 꿈으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when climbing is a job or a dream.

phrases.en: That climber went up the mountain alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산악인'과 비슷하지만 '등반가'는 높은 산을 오르는 행동에 더 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '산악인', but '등반가' focuses more on the act of climbing high mountains.

explain_en: It mainly refers to people who climb high mountains professionally or very seriously. For someone who just goes hiking casually, '등산객' sounds more natural. It is also often used in news to introduce famous climbers.

examples.en: He is a monk who lives in a mountain temple.
The monk wakes up every dawn to pray.

examples.ko: 영화에서 본 수도승의 삶이 인상 깊었어요.
examples.en: The life of the monk I saw in the movie was impressive.
I want to live quietly like a monk.
The monks are eating in silence.
He left his family to become a monk.

explain: 불교의 승려는 보통 '스님'이라고 불러요. '수도승'은 수도하며 사는 사람을 두루 가리키고, '수도사'라는 말도 있어요.

phrases.en: A monk appears in that movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수도승'과 같은 뜻으로, 서양 종교 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 수도승, but more common in Western religious contexts.

phrases.en: He became a monk when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삶의 선택을 말할 때 '이/가 되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 이/가 되다 to talk about a life choice.

phrases.en: He lives quietly like a monk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검소하고 조용한 생활을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a simple, quiet life.

explain_en: Buddhist monks are usually called '스님'. '수도승' refers broadly to people living a life of religious training, and '수도사' is another word for this.

examples.en: This year's Nobel Prize winners were announced.
The winners went up onto the stage.

examples.ko: 저는 그 영화제의 수상자를 만난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have met a winner of that film festival.
The top winner also gets prize money.
I cried after hearing the winner's speech.

examples.ko: 우리 반 친구가 대회 수상자로 뽑혔어요.
examples.en: A friend in my class was chosen as a competition winner.

explain: '수상자'는 상을 받은 사람이고, 뉴스나 시상식 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 시험이나 경기에서 이긴 사람은 '우승자', 상을 주는 쪽은 '시상자'라서 헷갈리지 않게 조심하세요. 말할 때는 보통 '상 받은 사람'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I checked the list of prize winners online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상을 받은 사람들의 이름을 모은 목록을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The list of names of those who won awards.

phrases.en: This year's grand prize winner is Mr. Kim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 큰 상을 받은 사람처럼 상의 이름과 함께 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the name of the prize, such as the grand prize.

phrases.en: Those who received a prize, please come forward.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수상자'보다 부드러운 말로, 일상 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, everyday way to say 수상자.

explain_en: 수상자 is a person who received a prize, common in news and award ceremonies. A winner of a match is 우승자, and the person who presents the prize is 시상자, so do not mix them up. In casual speech people also say 상 받은 사람.

examples.en: My father is a collector who gathers old coins.
The collector bought a rare stamp at a high price.

examples.ko: 저는 인형 수집가라서 집에 인형이 많아요.
examples.en: I'm a doll collector, so I have lots of dolls at home.
That collector's room is full of books.
The museum borrowed paintings from a collector.
Art collectors often visit exhibitions.

explain: 우표·동전·그림처럼 한 가지를 오래, 진지하게 모으는 사람에게 써요. 가볍게 모으는 사람은 그냥 '모으는 사람'이라고 해요. '우표 수집가'처럼 앞에 모으는 물건을 붙이고, 같은 뜻으로 '컬렉터'도 써요.

phrases.en: My grandfather is a famous stamp collector.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모으는 물건을 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the item being collected in front.

phrases.en: I went to an event where coin collectors gather.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-들'을 붙여 여러 사람을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -들 to talk about several collectors.

phrases.example: 그 컬렉터는 그림을 백 점 넘게 가지고 있어요.
phrases.en: That collector owns over a hundred paintings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수집가'와 같은 뜻인데, 미술품이나 비싼 물건에 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 수집가, but more common for art and valuable items.

explain_en: It is used for someone who seriously collects one kind of thing over a long time, such as stamps, coins or paintings. Someone who collects casually is just called '모으는 사람'. You put the collected item in front, as in '우표 수집가', and '컬렉터' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: The church has about three hundred members.
Worshippers going to the temple line up.
He was a member of this church for a long time.
I'm worried because the number of members shrinks every year.
They say many new members have joined.
A representative of the members gave a speech.

explain: 같은 종교를 믿고 그 교회나 절에 다니는 사람을 가리켜요. 비슷한 '신자'도 많이 써요. '불교 신도', '교회 신도'처럼 종교나 장소 이름 앞에 붙여 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: This cathedral has many believers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신도'와 뜻이 거의 같아요. 특히 성당(가톨릭)에서는 '신자'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as '신도'; '신자' is used especially often for Catholic churches.

phrases.en: He was a member of the church for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소 이름 앞에 붙여서 어느 곳에 다니는 사람인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attaching a place name shows which place the person attends.

phrases.en: Buddhist followers gathered at the temple.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종교 이름 앞에 붙여서 어떤 종교를 믿는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attaching a religion's name shows which religion the person follows.

explain_en: Refers to people who share a faith and attend a particular church or temple. The similar '신자' is also common. It can follow a religion or place name, as in '불교 신도' (Buddhist follower) or '교회 신도'.

en: all sorts of people; Tom, Dick and Harry; the rabble

examples.en: All sorts of random people gathered at that party.

examples.ko: 아무나 어중이떠중이를 다 뽑을 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't just hire any Tom, Dick or Harry.
That gathering is noisy because all kinds of people are there.

examples.ko: 어중이떠중이까지 다 나서니 일이 더 꼬였어요.
examples.en: With every Tom, Dick and Harry getting involved, things got even more tangled.
I'm not just some random person, I'm a real expert.

examples.ko: 어중이떠중이 말은 듣지 말고 직접 확인하세요.
examples.en: Don't listen to just anybody, check it yourself.

explain: 별 볼 일 없는 여러 사람을 한꺼번에 낮잡아 말할 때 써요. 사람을 낮추는 표현이라 상대방에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 돼요. 말하는 사람이 '내가 보기에 별로인 사람들'이라고 느낄 때 쓰는 말투예요.

phrases.en: A rabble of random people showed up and it was noisy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 여러 사람을 낮잡아 한꺼번에 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 들 refers to a whole crowd in a belittling way.

phrases.en: Don't gather just any random people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자격을 따지지 않고 사람을 모을 때 비판하는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A critical tone for gathering people without any standard.

phrases.en: Even every random person came, so there are no seats.
phrases.nuance_ko: '까지'를 붙여 별 볼 일 없는 사람들까지 모두 왔다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 까지 gives the sense that even the unremarkable people all came.

explain_en: It is used to look down on a crowd of ordinary or unimpressive people all at once. Because it belittles people, it is rude to use it directly about the person you are talking to. It reflects the speaker's feeling of 'people who don't impress me'.

examples.en: An elder of the academic world gave advice to juniors.
That actor is called a veteran of the film world.

examples.ko: 원로 가수의 공연에 많은 사람이 모였어요.
examples.en: Many people gathered for the veteran singer's concert.
I learned a lot listening to the elders' stories.

examples.ko: 우리 마을 원로께서 행사를 열어 주셨어요.
examples.en: An elder of our village held the event for us.
A veteran and a newcomer stood on stage together.

explain: '원로'는 한 분야에서 오래 일하고 존경받는 어른이에요. 보통 '원로 배우', '원로 가수', '원로 학자'처럼 직업 앞에 붙여요. 나이만 많은 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: A veteran actor received an award.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 활동하고 존경받는 배우를 높여 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful term for a long-active, esteemed actor.

phrases.en: An eminent senior scholar gave a lecture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학문 분야에서 오래 일한 존경받는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respected person with long years in academia.

phrases.en: I listened closely to the elder's advice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경험이 많은 어른의 말을 존중할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to respect the words of an experienced elder.

explain_en: '원로' is a respected senior figure with a long career in a field. It is usually put before a job, as in '원로 배우' or '원로 학자'. It isn't used for someone who is merely old.

examples.ko: 몽골의 유목민은 양과 말을 키우며 살아요.
examples.en: Mongolian nomads live raising sheep and horses.
Nomads move with each season in search of grass.

examples.ko: 유목민의 전통 집인 게르를 직접 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have seen a ger, the traditional home of nomads, in person.
I saw a nomad family in the desert in a documentary.

examples.ko: 요즘은 노트북 하나로 일하는 디지털 유목민도 있어요.
examples.en: These days there are even digital nomads who work with just a laptop.
For nomads, a horse is the most precious property.

explain: 풀을 따라 가축을 키우며 옮겨 다니는 사람들에게 써요. 한 곳에 사는 사람은 '정착민', 농사짓는 사람은 '농경민'이라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 소리 나는 대로 [유몽민]이라고 읽는 것도 주의하세요.

phrases.example: 이 다큐멘터리는 유목민의 삶을 보여 줘요.
phrases.en: This documentary shows the life of nomads.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '의'를 붙여 그 사람들의 생활을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 의 lets you talk about the nomads' way of life.

phrases.example: 몽골은 오래전부터 유목 민족이 살던 곳이에요.
phrases.en: Mongolia is a place where nomadic peoples have lived since long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람보다 집단이나 민족을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a whole people or group rather than an individual.

phrases.en: Unlike nomads, settled people live in one place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한곳에 머물러 사는 사람을 뜻하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The contrasting word for people who live in one place.

explain_en: It is used for people who move around raising livestock and following grass. It helps to learn it with '정착민' (settlers) and '농경민' (farming people). Also note the pronunciation [유몽민].

examples.en: Medical professionals must protect patients' information.
Healthcare workers really went through a lot during COVID.
I went to the nursing department to become a medical professional.

examples.ko: 의료인에게 감사 편지를 쓴 학생이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many students wrote thank-you letters to healthcare workers.

examples.ko: 이 행사는 의료인만 참석할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only medical professionals can attend this event.

examples.ko: 의료인 부족 문제가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: The shortage of medical professionals often appears in the news.

explain: '의료인'은 의사, 간호사처럼 병원이나 의료 일을 하는 사람들을 크게 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 한 직업만 말할 때는 '의사', '간호사'처럼 구체적으로 불러요. 뉴스나 공문서에서는 '의료인', '의료진'이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The hospital's medical staff took good care of the patients.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의료인'과 비슷하지만 한 병원이나 팀의 사람들을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 의료인, but used more for the staff of one hospital or team.

phrases.en: I want to become a medical professional.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 진로를 말할 때 '되다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 되다 when talking about dreams or careers.

phrases.en: I sent thanks to the medical professionals.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 여러 명을 말하고, 높일 때는 '께'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 들 makes it plural, and 께 is used to show respect.

explain_en: 의료인 is a broad word that groups doctors, nurses, and others who work in medicine. When you mean one job, you name it directly, such as 의사 or 간호사. The words 의료인 and 의료진 appear often in news and official documents.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 이민족의 침입을 막으려고 성을 쌓았어요.
examples.en: In the past, people built walls to stop invasions by other peoples.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 오랫동안 이민족에게 지배를 받았어요.
examples.en: That country was ruled by another people for a long time.
Living together with another ethnic group, the cultures blended.
People of other ethnic groups did business near the border.

examples.ko: 이민족을 차별하지 않는 사회를 만들어야 해요.
examples.en: We should build a society that doesn't discriminate against other ethnic groups.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 이민족이 세운 나라에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, I learned about a country founded by another people.

explain: 자기 민족과 다른 민족을 가리키는 말로, 역사나 뉴스 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 같은 민족은 '동족'이라고 하고, '이민자'는 다른 나라로 옮겨 사는 사람이라서 뜻이 달라요. '타민족'과 비슷하게 쓰지만 이민족이 조금 더 딱딱한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The walls were built to prepare for invasions by other peoples.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in historical contexts.

phrases.en: People of other ethnic groups live together in that country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷해요. 이민족은 역사 이야기에서 더 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning; 이민족 appears more often in historical contexts.

phrases.en: The general fought other peoples and protected the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '과'를 붙여 상대를 나타내는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the particle '과' to mark the opponent.

explain_en: It refers to a people different from your own ethnic group and mainly appears in history and news. People of the same ethnicity are '동족', and '이민자' means someone who moves to another country, so the meaning differs. It is used much like '타민족', though '이민족' feels a bit stiffer.

examples.en: A child should also be respected as an individual person.
Could a robot become a person with its own personality?

examples.ko: 부모는 자녀를 독립된 인격체로 대해야 해요.
examples.en: Parents should treat their children as independent individuals.

examples.ko: 그는 한 인격체로서 존중받고 싶다고 말했어요.
examples.en: He said he wanted to be respected as a person.
Many people treat their pets like persons.

examples.ko: 사람을 물건이 아니라 인격체로 보는 태도가 중요해요.
examples.en: It's important to see people as persons, not objects.

explain: '인격'은 사람의 됨됨이(인격이 훌륭하다)이고, '인격체'는 그런 인격을 가진 하나의 독립된 존재예요. '독립된 인격체', '인격체로 대하다'처럼 존중을 말할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.en: A child is an independent person, separate from the parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람을 따로 존중해야 하는 존재로 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used to say a person is a separate being deserving respect.

phrases.en: Please treat employees as individual people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 물건이 아니라 존중할 존재로 대한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means treating someone as a person to respect, not an object.

phrases.en: That teacher has an excellent character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 됨됨이를 말하는 말로, '인격체'보다 성품에 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person's character, focusing on traits rather than being a person.

explain_en: '인격' is a person's character (as in '인격이 훌륭하다'), while '인격체' is the independent being who has that character. It is common in phrases about respect, like '독립된 인격체' and '인격체로 대하다'.

examples.ko: 그 단체의 조직원이 천 명이 넘어요.
examples.en: That group has more than a thousand members.
A notice went out saying they're recruiting new members.
The members meet every Monday.

examples.ko: 경찰이 범죄 조직원 세 명을 붙잡았어요.
examples.en: The police caught three members of a criminal organization.
The union first asked its members for their opinions.

examples.ko: 그는 조직원으로서 맡은 일을 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: As a member, he worked hard at the task he was given.

explain: 뉴스에서는 범죄 조직이나 정치 단체의 사람을 말할 때 많이 나와요. 회사나 모임 사람은 '직원', '회원', '구성원'이 자연스러워요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않는 편이에요.

phrases.en: The members gathered and held a meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 조직의 여러 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '들' refers to several members of the group.

phrases.example: 그 단체는 새 조직원을 모집하고 있어요.
phrases.en: That group is recruiting new members.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 새로 뽑을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when taking in new people.

phrases.en: The police caught a criminal organization member.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 흔하게 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in the news.

explain_en: In the news it mostly refers to people in a criminal or political organization. For people in a company or club, '직원', '회원', or '구성원' sound more natural. It is rarely used in everyday conversation.

dis.h: member of an organization, often criminal

p.n: 조직원 sounds like a formal gang or organization member; 일원 is more neutral.

examples.ko: 검사 결과 그 아이는 두 사람의 친자로 확인됐어요.
examples.en: The test results confirmed that the child is the couple's biological child.

examples.ko: 친자 확인 소송 소식이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: News about a paternity suit came out on the news.
That child is not adopted but their biological child.

examples.ko: 친자와 양자를 차별하지 않는 부모도 많아요.
examples.en: Many parents don't treat their biological and adopted children differently.

examples.ko: 유전자 검사로 친자 여부를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can find out whether someone is a biological child through a DNA test.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 주인공이 친자가 아니라는 비밀이 밝혀져요.
examples.en: In the drama, the secret that the main character is not a biological child is revealed.

explain: 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 '친자 확인'처럼 자주 나오는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '친아들', '친딸', '친자식'처럼 말해요. 입양한 자녀는 '양자'라고 해서 짝으로 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: They did a paternity test at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스와 법 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in news and legal talk.

phrases.en: He is the boss's own son.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '친자' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: What people say in daily conversation instead of 친자.

phrases.en: I am my father's own daughter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '친아들'의 짝으로, 피가 이어진 딸을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 친아들, meaning a biological daughter.

explain_en: This word often appears in news and legal contexts, as in '친자 확인' (paternity/parentage test). In everyday talk people say '친아들', '친딸' or '친자식'. It pairs with '양자' (adopted child), so it helps to learn them together.

examples.ko: 한국에서는 학연과 지연이 중요하다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: In Korea, people say school ties and hometown ties matter.
A rumor went around that he got promoted because of school ties.
We came from the same school, so we grew close through that tie.

examples.ko: 채용은 학연이 아니라 실력으로 해야 해요.
examples.en: Hiring should be based on ability, not school ties.
He worked without playing up his school connections.

examples.ko: 학연에 얽매이지 않는 회사를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a company that isn't bound by school ties.

explain: 같은 학교를 나와서 생기는 인연이에요. 한국에서는 '학연, 지연, 혈연'을 한 묶음으로 자주 말하고, '학연으로 뽑다'처럼 불공평하다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요. 좋은 뜻으로는 '동문', '선후배'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: This company doesn't care about school ties.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 학교 출신인지 보고 판단한다는 뜻이고, 보통 부정적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means judging people by which school they attended, usually negatively.

phrases.en: Hiring people through school ties is unfair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불공평한 일을 비판할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to criticize unfair practices.

phrases.example: 저는 그 회사에 학연이 없어서 소개받기 어려웠어요.
phrases.en: I have no school ties to that company, so it was hard to get an introduction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 학교 출신 인맥이 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you have no connections from the same school.

explain_en: It is the connection formed by attending the same school. Koreans often group '학연, 지연, 혈연' (school, hometown, family ties) together, and '학연으로 뽑다' carries a tone of criticism about unfairness. For a positive meaning, '동문' or '선후배' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 우리 삼촌은 해병으로 군 생활을 했어요.
examples.en: My uncle served in the military as a marine.
The marine unit is near the coast.

examples.ko: 해병이 되려면 체력 시험을 통과해야 해요.
examples.en: To become a marine, you have to pass a fitness test.

examples.ko: 형이 해병에 지원해서 다음 달에 입대해요.
examples.en: My older brother applied to the marines and enlists next month.
The marines are training on the sand.
The marine in the movie looked really cool.

explain: 해병은 해군과 따로 있는 부대 사람이고, 바다에서 땅으로 올라가 싸우는 일을 맡아요. 군대 이야기에서는 '육군', '해군', '공군'과 함께 '해병대'라고도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: My older brother joined the Marine Corps last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해병'은 사람이고 '해병대'는 그 사람들의 부대 전체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: '해병' is a person, while '해병대' is the whole corps they belong to.

phrases.en: He is a former marine, so he is strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 해병이었던 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who used to be a marine.

phrases.example: 저는 군대에 가면 해병이 되고 싶어요.
phrases.en: If I go into the military, I want to become a marine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '되다'와 함께 써서 바라는 일이나 앞으로의 계획을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '되다' it expresses a wish or a future plan.

explain_en: 해병 is a member of the marine corps, which is separate from the navy and fights by landing from the sea. In talk about the military, people often say 해병대 (the Marine Corps) next to 육군, 해군, and 공군.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 혈연관계가 아니지만 친형제처럼 지내요.
examples.en: They aren't blood relatives, but they live like real brothers.
I heard they took a DNA test to confirm the blood relation.

examples.ko: 혈연관계가 없어도 가족이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can become a family even without blood ties.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 대부분 혈연관계로 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: Most people in this village are connected by blood ties.

examples.ko: 회사에서 혈연관계로 사람을 뽑으면 공정하지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't fair if a company hires people because of family ties.

examples.ko: 혈연관계보다 오래 함께 산 정이 더 중요할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes the bond from living together long matters more than blood relation.

explain: '혈연'은 피로 이어진 사이이고, '혈연관계'는 그 관계를 말해요. 같은 고향 사람끼리의 '지연', 같은 학교 출신끼리의 '학연'과 함께 '혈연·지연·학연'으로 묶어 말하는 경우가 많아요. 순우리말로는 '핏줄'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That person and I are not related by blood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '있다/없다'와 같이 써서 피가 이어졌는지를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'exist/not exist' to say whether there is a blood tie.

phrases.example: 혈연보다 친구가 더 가까울 때도 있어요.
phrases.en: Sometimes a friend is closer than a blood relative.
phrases.nuance_ko: '관계' 없이 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The short form without 'relationship'.

phrases.en: We look alike because we are of the same blood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순우리말이라서 대화에서 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native Korean word that sounds softer in conversation.

explain_en: '혈연' is a tie by blood, and '혈연관계' is that relationship. It is often grouped as '혈연·지연·학연' with '지연' (ties from the same hometown) and '학연' (ties from the same school). The native Korean word is '핏줄'.
